top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) is the best bounded discovery on the slate. Firm heterogeneity and selection changed the unit of analysis in trade from industries to firms and added a reallocation channel for the gains from trade that earlier new trade theory lacked. The mechanism has been tested on firm-level customs and production data for over twenty years. Two names match the core model and the broader firm-level agenda. I would word the citation around selection and reallocation, not welfare magnitudes, which are sensitive to elasticity assumptions. Remaining risks are the claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and the overlap with the 2008 trade prize, which I read as a different discovery. P002 (B015) ranks second because its influence and maturity are very large, but its three-name attribution is contestable and Calvo pricing is a device with mixed micro evidence. P004 (B050) has the cleanest attribution but thinner direct identification of the collateral channel and some thematic overlap with the 2022 prize. P003 (B036) has strong identification, but it bundles two strands and the third name is unsettled. Every proposal is a substantive scientific contribution, so no award ranks last. I judged on the record and not on support counts.
recusal_note: No profile-based tie to Melitz, Helpman, Redding, Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Dorn or Hanson. I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of committee members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart, and I treat their arguments as evidence only. I gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity; my field is political science, which is adjacent to B021, my former first choice and not on the slate. I am also least able to judge the technical trade and macroeconomic literatures. These ties are disclosed and not adjudicated.
